L4: Thu 11 Apr, 2024 - 4:43 AM ET
L5: Fitch Ratings - Barcelona - 11 Apr 2024: Fitch Ratings has published Ford Otomotiv Sanayi A.S.'s (Ford Otosan) Long-Term Foreign-
L6: Currency Issuer Default Rating (IDR) of 'BB+' with a Stable Outlook. Fitch has also assigned the company's proposed Eurobond an
L7: expected senior unsecured rating of 'BB+(EXP)/RR4'. Final ratings are subject to the completion of refinancing and final documentation
L8: confirming to information already received.
L9: The ratings and Outlook consider Ford Otosan's solid through-the-cycle financial profile, which Fitch views as largely in line with
L10: investment-grade automotive peers. The investment guarantee scheme embedded in the contract manufacturing agreement with Ford
L11: Motor Company (FMC, BBB-/Stable) helps protect Ford Otosan's revenue and margins from a market downturn and ensures complete
L12: capex recovery over the planned product cycle. We expect leverage metrics to closely follow the investment cycle and that the
L13: deleveraging path after the initial investment spike will be supported by healthy free cash flow (FCF) generation before dividend
L14: distribution.
L15: Ford Otosan's business profile is characterised by its small scale and limited diversification compared with auto peers, which Fitch views
L16: as constraining the rating. The nature of being a contract manufacturer implies little brand value although Ford-branded light
L17: commercial vehicles (LCVs) produced by Ford Otosan have a leading market position in Europe. The internal synergy and ability to fund
L18: R&D needs without tapping into FMC network is limited.

L23: KEY RATING DRIVERS
L24: Leading Europe Segment Market Share: Ford-branded commercial vehicles (CVs) have a leading position in Europe, which is expected
L25: to grow together with new product launches. Transit, including its variants, is leading European van unit sales. This translated into Ford
L26: Otosan's export revenues significantly increasing between 2015 and 2023. CV registration in Europe has rebounded strongly since the
L27: start of 2023 from a low base in 2022, but it remains below the pre-pandemic level.
L28: We expect demand for new CVs to remain strong as leisure and business services activities continue to recover, which will support high
L29: capacity utilisation levels of 80-90% at Ford Otosan's plants.
L30: Solid Through-the-Cycle Financial Profile: Ford Otosan's financial profile is commensurate with Fitch's expectation for low investment-
L31: grade automakers. An EBIT margin between 5%-6% places it comfortably against the high investment-grade median (6%) in our rating
L32: criteria for auto manufacturers. We forecast the FCF margins to remain negative to neutral over the rating horizon and EBITDA net
L33: leverage to hover around 2x, driven by funding needs to roll out a four-year product pipeline. Ford Otosan has a record of healthy cash
L34: flow generation, which gives the company deleveraging capacity once mass production starts.
L35: Investment Guarantee Scheme: As part of the contract manufacturing agreement, FMC provides Ford Otosan with an investment
L36: guarantee that secures a contractual volume despite actual sales volumes and enables Ford Otosan to recover upfront capex over the
L37: planned product cycle. The scheme also entails a cost-plus pricing mechanism that incorporates the full pass-through of the production
L38: expense and a profit mark-up. The investment guarantee scheme effectively serves as floor for Ford Otosan's revenue and earnings and
L39: offers some protection from a market downturn, which was evident by the resilient performance throughout the pandemic.
L40: Scale, Diversification Constrain Rating: Ford Otosan is considered small compared with European vehicle manufacturers including
L41: Volkswagen AG and Mercedes-Benz Group AG that also feature a much broader spectrum of vehicle types, brands, and models and are
L42: well-diversified geographically. With expected production capacity above 900,000 by 2025, Ford Otosan is among the top producers
L43: when compared with the LCV/van segments of Renault, Stellantis N.V., and VW.
L44: Consequently, we deem Ford Otosan a niche player despite its leading position in the covered markets and its size and scale constrain
L45: the rating at the current level. Additionally, Ford Otosan's engineering know-how and own intellectual property rights are largely

L64: Otosan also plays a pivotal role in FMC's global CV strategy and electrification roadmap. It will manufacture six out of nine FMC's future
L65: electric models, including E-Transit, E-Custom, and the flagship LCVs is set to be a key pillar of its electric vehicle arm.
L66: Rating Reflects Standalone Profile: As a JV, Ford Otosan's IDR currently reflects its Standalone Credit Profile (SCP). Fitch views the
L67: links between FMC and Ford Otosan as potentially supporting a one-notch rating uplift from Ford Otosan's SCP. This reflects our
L68: assessment using Parent and Subsidiary Linkage Rating Criteria (PSL) where we see operational and strategic incentives for FMC to
L69: support Ford Otosan, offset by the lack of debt guarantees or cross-default clauses.
L70: We have not applied any additional notching to Ford Otosan's IDR under the PSL as this would lead to rating equalisation with FMC,
L71: which we do not deem appropriate due to the existing JV structure and proximity of credit profiles. The rating uplift could be applicable
L72: if Ford Otosan's SCP weakens, if FMC guarantees bulk of its debt, or if FMC's ratings were upgraded.

L203: Company Description

L506: Covenants
L507: FO is subject to a financial covenant under its loan agreements with the European Bank for
L508: Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) and the International Finance Corporation (IFC), which
L509: stipulates that the group's consolidated reported net debt to EBITDA should not exceed 3.5x. This
L510: covenant is tested semi-annually on June 30 and December 31 of each year. The €435 million
L511: unsecured capex loan facility in Romania is also subject to a 3.5x reported net debt-to-EBITDA
L512: limit, based on the EBITDA generated by the FO Romania entity and debt at this level only. The
L513: planned bond issuance of up to $500 million is not subject to financial covenants.
L514: We expect comfortable headroom under the 3.5x consolidated net debt-to-EBITDA covenant
L515: requirement of the EBRD and IFC loan agreements in the next 12 months, and that FO will adjust
L516: the drawings of its Romania capex loan facility according to the EBITDA growth of the FO Romania
L517: entity, such that it maintains adequate headroom under the local covenant.
L518: Environmental, Social, And Governance
L519: Environmental factors are a negative consideration in our credit rating analysis of FO because it
L520: faces tight fuel efficiency and emissions targets in its main export European market (73% of 2023
L521: sales). We view the group's ability to meet regulatory standards in Europe as in line with that of
L522: many of its peers based on its portfolio plans.
L523: The company's electrification plans are driven by those of its key industrial shareholder and
L524: manufacturing partner, FMC, which targets to offer an all-electric fleet of vehicles in Europe by
L525: 2035 and to introduce new PC and CV electric models in 2024. FMC is also committed to achieving
L526: carbon neutrality no later than in 2050, and no later than 2035 in Europe.
L527: Overall, we believe that consumer acceptance of FO's EV products will be a key credit factor for
L528: assessing its competitive advantage, alongside its ability to maintain sound profitability on those
L529: products.

L535: We do not apply our recovery analysis to FO's capital structure due the material exposure of its

L539: subsidiary level, we expect that the vast majority of the company's debt will remain unsecured and

L541: below 50% sustainably, in line with the about 20% ratio we estimate pro-forma a full utilization of
L542: the capex loan at FO Romania.
L543: Analytical conclusions
L544: We rate the unsecured notes preliminary 'BB-', in line with our preliminary issuer credit rating,
L545: because we do not anticipate any significant subordination risk in the company's capital
